claim: For every integer n with 4 <= n <= 15 and every nonnegative n x n real matrix A whose entries sum to n, if phi(A) := prod_i r_i + prod_j c_j - per(A) >= 2 - n!/n^n and A has at least one zero entry, then lambda_2(A) := 1 - sigma_2(D_r^{-1/2} A D_c^{-1/2}) >= c_n, where sigma_2 is the second largest singular value, D_r and D_c are the diagonal matrices of the row and column sums, and c_n := 2 sqrt(gamma_n kappa_n)/theta_n with gamma_n = n!/n^n, h_n = sqrt(2 gamma_n), theta_n = 1 - h_n, kappa_n = 1/((1 - gamma_n)(1 - 2 h_n/3)).

quadruple.statement: For every integer n with 4 <= n <= 15 and every nonnegative n x n real matrix A whose entries sum to n, if phi(A) := prod_i r_i + prod_j c_j - per(A) >= 2 - n!/n^n and A has at least one zero entry, then lambda_2(A) := 1 - sigma_2(D_r^{-1/2} A D_c^{-1/2}) >= c_n, where sigma_2 is the second largest singular value, D_r and D_c are the diagonal matrices of the row and column sums, and c_n := 2 sqrt(gamma_n kappa_n)/theta_n with gamma_n = n!/n^n, h_n = sqrt(2 gamma_n), theta_n = 1 - h_n, kappa_n = 1/((1 - gamma_n)(1 - 2 h_n/3)).
quadruple.stage: spectral geometry of nonnegative matrices near the doubly stochastic polytope: one finite-dimensional statement per n, about the second singular value of a normalised matrix

shape.objects: A ranges over a compact semialgebraic subset of K_n (the simplex of nonnegative n x n matrices with entry sum n) cut out by phi(A) >= 2 - gamma_n and a_ij = 0 for some (i,j); finite-dimensional, dimension n^2 - 2 for each fixed zero position. n ranges over 4..15 but the statement is natural for all n.
shape.quantifiers: universal over A, for each fixed n; the conclusion is a single scalar inequality. There is no existential inside.
shape.target_quantity: an explicit constant c_n (about 0.183 at n = 7 down to 0.0035 at n = 15, of order sqrt(gamma_n) = sqrt(n!/n^n)); the true value appears to be an absolute constant near 0.7 by numerical evidence, so a very lossy proof suffices.
shape.ambient_structure: three kinds of structure coexist: the multilinear algebra of the permanent, the convex geometry of the doubly stochastic polytope (Birkhoff), and the spectral theory of the normalised bipartite adjacency operator. The simpler ambient that keeps the constraint is the doubly stochastic polytope Omega_n itself, since a near-maximiser is within sqrt(2 gamma_n) of it in every row and column sum.
shape.symmetries: invariant under G_n = (S_n x S_n) semidirect Z_2 (row permutations, column permutations, transpose); both phi and lambda_2 are G_n-invariant, and the hypothesis 'has a zero entry' is too.
shape.configuration: the forbidden configuration is a near-decomposition: lambda_2 small means, by Cheeger, a sparse cut of the bipartite graph, that is a set S of rows and T of columns with |S| + |T| ~ n and little mass in S x T^c. It is not an algebraic relation.
shape.extremal_candidate: the Knopp-Sinkhorn extremal T_n (the doubly stochastic matrix with one zero, 1/(n-1) on the rest of its row and column, (n-2)/(n-1)^2 elsewhere) is the minimiser of per on the boundary of Omega_n; its lambda_2 is bounded away from 0 uniformly in n. Numerically the minimiser of lambda_2 subject to per <= 1.05 gamma_n is also near T_n, with lambda_2 about 0.70.
shape.finite_certificates: the false side has a finite certificate: a single matrix A with phi(A) >= 2 - gamma_n, a zero entry and lambda_2(A) < c_n, checkable in exact arithmetic. The true side has none in general (a universal statement over a continuum), except through an sum-of-squares certificate at fixed n, which is the route the Dittert attack already exhausted.
shape.monotonicity: c_n decreases like sqrt(gamma_n), so the statement gets weaker as n grows; the hardest case is the smallest n. The smallest open n is 7 (n = 4, 5, 6 are settled for the Dittert conjecture by other means, and the theorem is vacuous at n = 4 since c_4 > 1).
shape.uniformity_parameter: n. A proof with an absolute constant c independent of n implies every case, since c_n <= c_5 = 0.61 < 0.7.
shape.proof_shape: the natural shape is a contrapositive chain: lambda_2(A) small => (Cheeger) a sparse cut of the bipartite graph of A => A is close to block diagonal after permutations => per(A) >= per of the blocks, which for a k by k and an (n-k) by (n-k) block is at least gamma_k gamma_{n-k} = gamma_n sqrt(2 pi k(n-k)/n)(1+o(1)) >> gamma_n => phi(A) < 2 - gamma_n. Each step loses a constant; the loss to control is in Cheeger (a square root) and in the block bound (the cross terms).
shape.neighbours: van der Waerden inequality per(B) >= gamma_n on Omega_n with equality only at J_n/n (Egorychev, Falikman 1981): known true, this is the n = 0 case of the stability question. Knopp-Sinkhorn: min of per on the boundary of Omega_n is m_n = (n-2)!((n-2)/(n-1)^2)^{n-2}, attained at T_n: known true. Cheeger inequality for the normalised bipartite Laplacian: known true. Schrijver's inequality and the capacity method (Gurvits): known true. Quantitative stability of the van der Waerden inequality (per(B) <= (1+eta) gamma_n implies B close to J_n/n in some norm): open, not found in print. Alexandrov-Fenchel equality cases and their stability: partially known, hard.
shape.known_bounds: Cheon-Wanless 2012 Thm 2.1: a near-maximiser has every k-subset row and column sum within sqrt(2 delta k) of k, delta <= gamma_n; Thm 3.2: a maximiser is fully indecomposable; Thm 3.7: its zeros do not form a single block. These give qualitative non-decomposability but no spectral gap. Numerically (deterministic/numerical-optimisation-run-4 of the sibling attack): minimising lambda_2 over doubly stochastic matrices with a zero and per <= 1.05 gamma_n gives 0.697, 0.696, 0.726, 0.733 at n = 5, 6, 7, 8, against required 0.612, 0.323, 0.183, 0.108; in 1200 random samples per <= 1.05 gamma_n forced lambda_2 >= 0.71, 0.78, 0.86 at n = 5, 8, 12. The documented ceiling of the qualitative results is that they give no quantitative gap at all.
shape.missing_input: a quantitative form of the van der Waerden equality case: an explicit function f with per(B) <= (1 + eta) gamma_n implying dist(B, J_n/n) <= f(eta), in a norm strong enough to control the second singular value. Equivalently, a lower bound on per(B) in terms of the spectral gap of B.
shape.base_theory: ZFC; the statement is a sentence of the first-order theory of real closed fields for each fixed n, hence decidable in principle but not in practice (n^2 variables). No hypothesis beyond ZFC bears on it.

known: per(B) >= n!/n^n on the doubly stochastic polytope with equality only at J_n/n: Egorychev (1981), Falikman (1981).

Minimum of the permanent on the boundary of the doubly stochastic polytope, n > 3, is m_n = (n-2)!((n-2)/(n-1)^2)^{n-2}, attained at T_n: Knopp and Sinkhorn, Linear Multilinear Algebra 11 (1982) 351-355, doi:10.1080/03081088208817459.

A near-maximiser of phi has every k-subset row and column sum within sqrt(2 delta k) of k, and is fully indecomposable: Cheon and Wanless, Linear Algebra Appl. 436 (2012) 791-801, doi:10.1016/j.laa.2010.08.041, Thms 2.1 and 3.2.
The capacity proof of the van der Waerden inequality and its refinements: Gurvits (2006); Gurvits and Leake, arXiv:1804.04351.
Theorem R of the sibling attack: G(n, c_n) implies Dittert's conjecture at n; study/route-a-reduction-theorem.md of attack/dittert-conjecture-n5-to-n15 (2026-09-03).
